When considering medical care in China, you need practical answers: Is treatment in China suitable for my condition? What might it cost? Which treatment options are feasible?
We offer two assessment options for different information needs, helping you objectively understand your circumstances for seeking treatment.
Important: online assessments are preliminary guidance for treatment in China and do not replace an in-person diagnosis. The final treatment plan follows the doctor's conclusions after consultation and complete examinations at the hospital.
I. Two assessment options
Completely free initial assessment (no medical records required)
For patients who have not yet organized complete medical documents and want an initial overview.
Enter only basic information: your country, condition type, a brief description and your treatment goals. No imaging or medical record uploads are required.
This assessment can help you understand:
1. Basic suitability of treatment in China for your condition
2. An indicative overall budget range covering medical care, medicines and living in China, with an estimated budget ceiling
3. General comparison of similar treatments in China and abroad
4. Estimated duration of your stay in China
Without complete medical records and imaging, the free assessment provides only a broad reference and cannot give a precise treatment plan or clinical prognosis. Choose an in-depth expert assessment for a more detailed analysis.
In-depth expert assessment (complete medical records required)
For patients with complete medical documents who want a more detailed professional assessment to support treatment decisions.
Upload complete medical records, original DICOM images and laboratory reports. You may first use the Medical Record Translation and Organization Tool to standardize your documents and improve assessment accuracy.
The in-depth specialist assessment includes:
1. Objective prognosis reference
Based on your condition, stage and treatment history, describe clinical control in comparable cases and explain treatment opportunities and limitations honestly, without overstating outcomes.
2. Overview of potential treatment pathways
Specialists assess whether surgery, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy or other options are available and outline feasible treatment steps.
3. Cost estimates by category:
• Medical care: Estimates for examinations, hospitalization, surgery, treatment, beds and nursing
• Medication: Estimates for treatment drugs, targeted agents, immunotherapy and supportive medicines
• Living in China: Estimates for accommodation, meals and companion transport
• A capped budget for the entire treatment, specifying no extra hidden charges.
4. Matched hospital recommendations with comparisons of suitability
5. Comparison of treatment options across countries
6. Treatment risk alerts and medical issues requiring particular attention
7. Required document checklist and scheduling advice for treatment in China
II. Preparing assessment documents
1. Free preliminary assessment: complete the basic form; no medical records or imaging uploads required.
2. For an in-depth expert assessment, prepare:
• Diagnostic reports, pathology reports and discharge summaries
• Original DICOM images and reports from CT, MRI and PET‑CT
• Complete laboratory and tumor marker test results
• All previous treatment records, including surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy and radiotherapy
• Current physical condition and a complete list of medications being taken
The more complete your documents, the more closely the specialist's prognosis reference, cost estimate and treatment pathway analysis can reflect your circumstances.
III. The complete assessment process
1. Choose assessment: Free initial assessment / In-depth expert assessment
2. Free initial assessment: Enter basic information for preliminary reference results
3. In-depth expert assessment: upload medical documents; you may standardize your records first
4. The medical team verifies and files the documents
5. A relevant specialist reviews all records and issues an assessment
6. Receive a complete assessment report
7. A medical concierge helps explain the report and answer questions about visas, insurance, travel and related matters
IV. Medical record privacy and security
All submitted records, images and personal medical information follow the same privacy protection standards:
1. Identity information is masked throughout and accessible only to the medical team involved in the assessment
2. Medical records and images will not be disclosed externally, displayed as case studies or used commercially
3. After the assessment service, all cloud backups can be permanently deleted at your request
4. Processes meet international GDPR and HIPAA privacy requirements
V. Start your assessment
Choose the free preliminary review for an overview of treatment requirements and budget in China, or the in-depth expert assessment for a detailed specialist analysis of your condition.

For patients from Muslim countries such as Indonesia, care in China involves not only treatment but also faith and daily customs. We respect Islamic culture and provide tailored support.
Partner JCI hospitals offer halal meals, with ingredients, preparation and utensils meeting Halal requirements. Meat is traceable; separate cookware prevents cross-contamination. Indonesian-style meals can be delivered to wards three times daily; nearby halal restaurants serve families.
Hospitals provide a separate prayer room (Musalla) with Qibla markings, ablution facilities and prayer mats; mats and direction guidance are also available in wards.
Staff coordinate examinations and surgery to avoid the five daily prayer times where possible; on Fridays, transport can be arranged to a nearby mosque for congregational prayer.
Respecting Islamic privacy practices, women may preferentially book female doctors and nurses. Examination rooms and wards have private changing screens; male staff knock and seek permission before entering. All-female teams can be arranged for gynecological care.
During Ramadan, we adjust care to the patient's condition, aim to schedule outside fasting hours and offer customized suhoor/iftar meals. Doctors assess fitness to fast and advise honestly if unsuitable; medicines and infusions can be scheduled around Ramadan routines.
Indonesian and Arabic medical interpreters support consultations, surgical discussions and instructions. Faith-related needs are proactively confirmed on admission and incorporated into care.
In extreme circumstances, we can help contact a mosque and arrange Islamic funeral procedures in line with the family's religious wishes.
We respect both medical needs and religious customs so Muslim patients can receive treatment abroad with peace of mind.

Overseas patients place great importance on the privacy of their records and health data, particularly those from the EU and Southeast Asia, where data protection requirements are strict.
We strictly follow GDPR and HIPAA international data protection standards, applying tiered safeguards to overseas patients' medical data:
• Only authorized medical personnel may access patients' medical records, imaging and personal identification information;
• Patient health data will not be disclosed or sold to third parties without the patient's written consent.
• Patients have the right to request and export their complete medical records;
• Medical data are encrypted during storage and transmission to reduce the risk of data breaches.
When patients need records for follow-up at home or insurance claims, we provide compliant electronic or paper reports as requested, safeguarding data throughout.
Aligned with international data protection rules to keep overseas patients' personal health information secure and under control.

A primary concern for many international patients planning treatment in China is whether Chinese hospitals meet international standards and are recognized worldwide.
JCI (Joint Commission International) is an internationally recognized healthcare quality and safety accreditation system, applying uniform global standards with no country-specific versions.
Among our partner institutions, 137 are JCI-accredited, aligning patient safety, care pathways, surgical quality control, infection prevention and nursing standards with internationally accepted requirements.
Published statistics report an inpatient infection rate of 0.5% at these JCI-accredited hospitals, compared with a 1.2% average in European and US hospitals, supported by stricter aseptic controls and postoperative safety systems.
From preoperative assessment and surgery to postoperative monitoring, care follows international protocols used in Europe, the US and Singapore. JCI accreditation helps overseas patients assess hospital legitimacy and safety.
JCI accreditation is more than promotion: it indicates that a hospital's safety system meets uniform international standards, providing a foundation for safe cross-border care.

Many international patients preparing for treatment in China face the same challenge:
Foreign-language records can be disorganized, formats vary between countries, images are scattered and medical terminology creates barriers.
This prevents specialists in China from quickly understanding the records and accurately assessing the condition, prolonging assessment and delaying care.
We offer patients from every country a one-stop service for translating and structurally organizing medical records.
Bring your overseas medical documents up to the review standards of specialists at China's top-tier tertiary hospitals.
I. What we can organize and translate for you
Covering all conditions and overseas medical document types worldwide, with no need for patients to select or organize files themselves:
1. Written diagnostic documents
Discharge summaries, specialist diagnoses, pathology and biopsy reports, previous treatment records, follow-up summaries and outpatient records.
2. Imaging records
Organize and archive imaging reports and original files from CT, MRI, PET-CT, X-ray and ultrasound examinations.
3. Laboratory results
Organize and cross-reference complete blood counts, tumor markers, liver and kidney function, targeted screening and all laboratory results.
4. Medication and treatment records
Organize records of targeted therapies, chemotherapy, pain medicines, long-term chronic-disease medicines and previous surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy.
All documents receive medical-grade Chinese translation, standardized formatting and structured archiving to fit China's healthcare system.

A visa is an essential part of preparing for treatment in China. Many international patients are unsure which visa to choose, what documents to prepare or how long processing takes; errors can delay medical appointments.
Please note: this article summarizes policies and document preparation only; it does not replace consular approval. Final entry and exit rules depend on current policies of Chinese embassies, consulates and customs.
I. Visa types for medical travel
International patients traveling to China for short-term care, inpatient surgery or postoperative follow-up may apply for an S2 visa. Unlike tourist or business visas:
1. This visa allows admission for legitimate medical care
2. A stay duration suited to your treatment needs
3. Immediate family can apply for companion visas and enter with the patient
II. Required documents · Patient
1. Original passport valid for more than 6 months
2. Recent ID photo with a white background
3. Proof of nationality and identity
4. Complete the visa application form
5. Treatment invitation from a medical institution in China (we assist with issuance)
6. Statement of purpose for medical travel
III. Supporting medical documents
1. Brief medical history
2. Recent diagnostic reports
3. Hospital appointment and acceptance confirmation
We can organize and archive your complete medical documents for direct use in your visa application.
IV. Family companion visa documents
Immediate family may apply for companion visas together; required documents:
1. Family member's passport and ID photo
2. Proof of family relationship
3. Proof of the patient's treatment and hospital invitation letter
V. Indicative processing times
1. Standard processing: 3–7 business days
2. Peak processing periods: 7–10 working days
3. Eligible applicants may request expedited processing
Once treatment is scheduled, begin preparing visa documents 1–2 weeks in advance to avoid delaying admission.
VI. Points to keep in mind
1. The S2 medical visa is for treatment and recovery only; employment in China is prohibited
2. The final visa approval determines the permitted stay in China
3. If travel plans change, we can help reissue medical documentation
4. All supplied documents are legitimate; we do not prepare false documentation
VII. Document pre-review assistance
We can check all your documents to reduce omissions:
1. Assistance obtaining a medical invitation letter
2. Medical document organization and filing
3. Pre-review of the document checklist
4. Step-by-step process guidance
VIII. Go to visa assistance
After checking your basic information, visit the visa assistance section to submit documents for preliminary review and arrange further support.

For international patients, treatment in China involves documents, assessment, visas, travel, hospital care and follow-up. Understanding the full process in advance reduces unexpected problems and makes care smoother.
Please note: this process is a reference guide. Appointment times and treatment arrangements may change according to your condition and hospital bed availability.
I. Preparing your records
1. Collect and organize all previous medical records, examination reports, imaging and medication records
2. Use the medical record translation tool to standardize and archive foreign-language records
3. Request a treatment feasibility assessment, choosing a free preliminary review or an in-depth expert assessment
4. Use the assessment to confirm whether treatment in China suits your circumstances and check insurance claim eligibility at the same time
II. Visa and travel preparation
1. After receiving the assessment, obtain the hospital invitation and other medical documents required for the visa
2. Visit visa assistance to prepare all S2 medical visa documents
3. Submit your visa application and await the decision
4. Confirm treatment dates; the platform can help book flights and accommodation together, while family members apply for accompanying visas.
III. Entry and arrival in China
1. Enter with a valid S2 medical visa and cooperate with customs checks
2. Arrive in the destination city and settle in
3. The medical concierge coordinates airport pickup, accommodation and local transport
IV. Treatment at the hospital
After admission, we provide a medical concierge and a daily-life concierge for support throughout:
Medical concierge (professionally qualified)
1. Help with registration, appointment accompaniment and attending-doctor coordination
2. Join clinical discussions, help confirm treatment plans and communicate patient concerns
3. Track treatment progress and share examination and treatment updates
4. Help organize and retain all medical documents for later insurance claims
Daily living coordinator
1. Handles daily arrangements: accommodation, meals, transport, interpretation and other practical needs
2. Handle daily hospital errands to ease the burden on patients and families
Our concierge team assists throughout hospital registration, appointment coordination, treatment discussions and related arrangements.
5. Follow-up after treatment and returning home
Online follow-up continues after you return home, supported by a medical concierge and doctor's assistant:
1. Medication reminders and home rehabilitation guidance
2. Messages answered within 24 hours, with ongoing recovery follow-up
3. Any unusual symptoms are promptly shared with your treating doctor in China for timely assessment.
VI. Common considerations
1. Complete a treatment assessment before buying flights to China to avoid a wasted journey if treatment is unsuitable or no beds are available
2. Keep original medical documents safely wherever possible; they are needed for insurance claims and follow-up
3. Treatment decisions rest with the in-person doctor in China; online assessments are for reference only
4. If travel or treatment plans change, contact your medical concierge for help making adjustments
VII. Start planning your treatment in China
To follow this process, start with organizing your records or a treatment assessment, then complete your care plan step by step.

For regular medicines brought by overseas patients, we help check ingredients and assess whether use can continue during treatment. Clinical staff monitor patients' responses to medication throughout care.
All medications and supplies used have complete quality certification, preventing products of unknown origin from entering clinical use.
Comprehensive traceability oversight and multiple pharmacy checks safeguard medication use for international patients in China.

s_jrxafl_1e2nkp2:
For Muslim patients worldwide, cross-border care involves more than treatment outcomes.
Respect for faith, halal food, a quiet prayer environment and observance of customary restrictions are essential to the care experience.
We specialize in supporting Muslim patients worldwide seeking treatment in China, with full respect for Islamic culture and customs.
This comprehensive, practical guide to medical care and daily life for Muslim patients supports reassuring treatment, comfortable living and religious observance in China.
Please note: all religious customs and cultural restrictions are respected throughout; services prioritize patients' practices without coercion or interruption.
I. Halal food throughout your stay
We help patients and families maintain a fully halal diet throughout, free of pork, lard and alcohol.
1. Halal food arrangements at your accommodation
• Prioritize apartments with cooking facilities and private kitchens for preparing halal meals
• Help purchase halal ingredients, staples, cooking oil and seasonings
• Keep non-halal ingredients separate throughout and prevent cross-contact
2. Halal dining assistance outside the hospital
• The concierge connects you with legitimate halal restaurants and Muslim canteens near the hospital
• Recommend locally certified halal shops for compliant, reassuring dining
• Help arrange regular halal meal deliveries for long-term needs
3. Dietary arrangements during hospital treatment
During hospitalization, the medical concierge informs nurses and dietitians in advance:
• Avoid pork, lard, alcohol-containing additives and prohibited ingredients throughout
• Adjust meal times flexibly for Ramadan and dietary habits
• All postoperative nutrition and recovery meals are halal
II. Prayer facilities and religious practices
Respect daily prayers and routines, providing a quiet, clean and private prayer environment.
1. Private prayer space in your accommodation
Arrange a quiet, clean room without interruptions or clutter to support five daily prayers.
2. Directions to nearby mosques
Our concierge provides locations and opening hours of established mosques near the hospital and accommodation,
and helps arrange transport for Friday congregational and holiday prayers.
3. Flexible medical scheduling
• Consultations, examinations and treatment can be scheduled around prayer times
• During Ramadan, appointments can be adjusted around sunrise and sunset
• No unwanted interruptions during treatment
III. Care during Ramadan
Tailored support for Ramadan fasting, fluid restrictions and special daily routines:
1. During daytime fasting, prioritize rest and noninvasive examinations where possible
2. Prioritize scheduling blood draws, infusions and specialized treatments after iftar
3. The concierge prepares iftar supplies, drinking water and light halal meals in advance
4. Help doctors adjust medication timing to physical condition
IV. Medical considerations and restrictions
Strictly respect Muslim patients' cultural restrictions and healthcare practices throughout:
1. Gender-appropriate care
On request, we can prioritize doctors and nurses of the same gender for examinations and nursing care, respecting privacy and gender-related customs.
2. Maximum privacy protection
Protect bodily privacy during examinations, treatment and dressing changes, minimizing exposure and respecting religious privacy requirements.
3. Screening medicines and supplies for prohibited ingredients
Your medical coordinator checks in advance:
• Medicines free of pork extracts and prohibited gelatin ingredients
• Compliant infusions and supplies without prohibited ingredients
• Discuss religious restrictions with doctors in advance to avoid discomfort
V. Clothing, daily life and festivals
1. Respect headscarves and traditional dress, which are permitted throughout the hospital
2. Dedicated daily-life support during Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
3. Help purchase daily essentials, religious items and prayer supplies
4. The daily-life concierge understands, adapts to and respects patients' routines throughout
6. Dual-concierge service dedicated to Muslim patients
We understand Muslim customs, medical sensitivities and cultural differences, providing attentive support throughout:
1. Medical care coordinator
• Understand religious restrictions and discuss them with doctors in advance
• Adjust treatment, examinations and medication around prayer and Ramadan schedules
• Protect privacy, respect customs and accommodate religious needs throughout
2. Daily living coordinator
• Halal food arrangements throughout
• Arrange a quiet prayer space and provide mosque directions
• Adapt to routines, holidays and dietary habits
• Support with cross-cultural daily life
VII. Personalized treatment advice for Muslim patients
For halal-friendly accommodation, Ramadan arrangements, same-gender clinicians, prayer spaces, restricted-medicine checks or holiday treatment scheduling, use our dedicated consultation channel for a personalized Muslim patient care plan.

Many international patients taking long-term medicines for chronic disease, targeted therapies or pain relief have concerns before treatment in China:
Can I bring my regular medicines into China? What quantity is permitted? Must I declare them? Could they be confiscated?
To help patients worldwide enter smoothly without interrupting medicines or treatment, we have compiled clear, practical medicine-entry standards aligned with official requirements and China's Measures for the Administration of Drug Importation.
Please note: this guide concerns lawful personal medical use and is for travel reference only. Final entry decisions depend on on-site customs inspection.
I. Core rules for bringing medicines into China (the sole customs assessment standard)
All personally carried medicines must follow two mandatory entry rules:
1. For personal use only: solely for treating your own condition; sale, purchase on behalf of others or transfer to others is prohibited.
2. Reasonable quantities: bring amounts consistent with your stay in China and treatment duration; do not stockpile excess supplies.
Standard chronic-disease medicines, targeted cancer drugs and postoperative recovery medicines may be carried legally when quantities are reasonable and for personal use.
II. Required entry documents to avoid detention of medicines
To help your personal medicines clear customs, prepare the following documents in advance:
1. Original prescription from a licensed doctor in your country
2. Relevant medicine leaflets and packaging
3. Personal diagnostic report
4. Proof of long-term medication (if applicable)
All documents establish that the medicines are necessary for your condition, taken long term and carried in reasonable quantities for personal use
III. Medicines that must be proactively declared
Declare the following medicines proactively at customs to reduce inspection risks:
1. Painkillers, sedatives and sleeping medicines
2. Psychotropic and controlled prescription medicines
3. High-dose hormonal medicines
4. Special targeted or specialist medications taken frequently over the long term
Proactive declaration and complete documents generally allow smooth clearance.
4. Items prohibited or strictly restricted at entry
1. Controlled anesthetics and narcotics containing prohibited ingredients
2. Unapproved overseas homemade or folk remedies with unknown ingredients
3. Stockpiled medicines in large quantities, without prescriptions or an explainable purpose
4. Noncompliant with China's entry standards. V. Medication guidance for patients coming to China
V. Short-term treatment in China
We recommend carrying only a 7–10-day transitional supply for entry. Remaining treatment medicines can be formally prescribed at hospitals in China, safely and lawfully, avoiding entry-related concerns.
VI. Patients on long-term chronic disease maintenance
Bring a sufficient quantity consistent with your prescription, keeping all medicines in their original outer packaging for customs inspection.
VII. Special medicines during treatment
For oncology and critical-care medicines, we can help prepare documents confirming treatment in China in advance. VI. Medication privacy
All patient medication information and condition-specific medicine lists remain strictly confidential throughout:
1. Visible only to the medical team; not published or used in case displays
2. Strict adherence to international privacy standards
3. Sensitive personal medication data is neither recorded nor shared externally

For patients with serious or chronic conditions or undergoing surgery, traveling to China with family offers reassurance. Families often ask: Can we enter together? Which visa is needed? Where can we stay? Can we accompany the patient in hospital? Is daily life in China convenient?
This complete guide for patients' families worldwide covers visas, travel, accommodation, hospital accompaniment and daily-life assistance for worry-free support throughout treatment.
Please note: accompaniment policies and visa rules depend on current consular and hospital requirements. This guide is a practical reference, with assistance throughout implementation.
1. Family companion visa guidance (can be arranged together)
Immediate family members (spouse, parents and children) may apply simultaneously for an S2 visa to accompany the patient for medical care.
1. No separate treatment certificate is needed; the patient's medical documents are sufficient
2. Visa stay duration can align with the treatment period
3. Multiple immediate family members may apply; accompaniment is not limited to one person
4. We help coordinate family accompaniment certificates and hospital
II. Documents required for family members visiting China
1. Family member's passport valid for more than 6 months
2. ID photo with a white background
3. Proof of family relationship
4. Patient treatment certificate and hospital acceptance letter (provided by us)
5. Visa application form
Our team helps pre-review documents throughout to reduce visa rejection and additional-document risks.
III. Flights and accommodation for family members
Family members need not plan their China itinerary alone; our platform provides a managed, one-stop booking service:
1. International flight booking assistance
Match return flights to the patient's treatment schedule, with flexibility to adjust the return date.
2. Accommodation inside or outside the hospital
Accommodation matched to your medical needs:
• Severely ill and surgical patients: Prioritize hospital companion rooms or nearby apartments
• Routine-care patients: Arrange safe, quiet residential accommodation with convenient amenities
• All accommodation is clean, safe and close to medical care,
IV. Accompaniment in China · Two concierge services throughout (for patients and families)
Family members arriving in China need not worry about language barriers, unfamiliar surroundings or medical procedures.
We provide both patients and families with two concierge services:
1. Medical concierge (licensed medical professional):
• Accompaniment throughout consultations, ward rounds and treatment planning
• Interpret clinical discussions so families understand the full treatment rationale
• Track daily treatment progress, test results and medication
• Coordinate with the attending doctor, ask questions on your behalf and share updates
• Organize all medical bills, records and claim documents
• Avoid treatment misconceptions and promptly flag changes in condition
2. Daily living coordinator:
Dedicated to all daily-life needs of patients and their families:
• Grocery shopping and everyday supplies
• Transport arrangements and transfers
• Everyday interpreting and help with local errands
• Accommodation upkeep and help with daily errands
• Help arrange meals suited to dietary preferences
Family members can focus on being with the patient while our team handles all practical details.
V. Hospital companion policies
1. Licensed hospitals in China allow immediate family to accompany inpatients
2. Family may accompany patients through surgery, chemotherapy and follow-up visits
3. Family may stay overnight so patients need not remain alone
4. If a companion must leave or be replaced, the concierge can temporarily
VI. Family life in China
To keep family members comfortable and stress-free while accompanying patients:
1. Help with internet access, household payments and local trips
2. Provide city living guidance and directions to shops, pharmacies and local amenities
3. Overcome language and communication barriers
4. 24-hour access for unexpected daily-life issues
VII. Flexible companion arrangements
To keep family members comfortable and stress-free while accompanying patients:
1. Short-term treatment: Family may stay throughout until discharge
2. Long-term treatment: family members can rotate flexibly; we help prepare documents for re-entry
3. If you need to return home during treatment, the concierge can independently follow the patient's care and keep family members updated in real time
VIII. Dedicated consultation for accompanying family members
To check a family member's visa eligibility, required documents, accommodation and length of accompaniment, use the dedicated consultation channel for a personalized family support plan.
